geography: Fram Formation, southern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, Canada

regionalRanges.label: Fram Formation occurrence
regionalRanges.region: Fram Formation, southern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, Canada
regionalRanges.basis: The regional record is tied to the Fram Formation specimens and rounded approximately 375 Ma age reported in the primary description.

overview: A Frasnian elpistostegalian known from articulated material that combines fish-like features with a mobile neck, robust ribs and a fin containing wrist-like joints.
evidenceSummary: Named Fram Formation specimens and primary descriptions strongly support the anatomical mosaic; direct ancestry and habitual terrestrial walking are not claimed.

title.en: A Devonian tetrapod-like fish and the evolution of the tetrapod body plan
title.zh: A Devonian tetrapod-like fish and the evolution of the tetrapod body plan

title.en: The pectoral fin of Tiktaalik roseae and the origin of the tetrapod limb
title.zh: The pectoral fin of Tiktaalik roseae and the origin of the tetrapod limb

scope.en: The selected anatomical, relationship or time-estimate material described in this account; no complete species history or distribution is inferred.
scope.zh: 用于本文选取的解剖、关系或时间估计材料，不由此推断完整物种史或分布。

text.zh: 提塔利克鱼的胸鳍保留鳍条，同时具有腕状关节；可活动的颈部与粗壮肋骨也出现在这具身体上。这些结构怎样联系鱼鳍与四肢？化石展示的是一组共存的解剖特征，运动能力与日常行为还需要分别解释。
text.en: Tiktaalik retains fin rays alongside wrist-like joints, a mobile neck and robust ribs. How does this combination connect fins and limbs? The fossil records anatomy in one body; movement capabilities and everyday behaviour require separate interpretation.

title.en: Scales, fin rays and wrist-like joints

text.zh: 提塔利克鱼的化石保留了鳞片和鳍条，也显示出可活动的颈部、粗壮的肋骨，以及带有类似腕部关节的胸鳍。它的意义在于：这些通常被我们分开讨论的结构，曾经可以出现在同一具身体上。
text.en: Tiktaalik retains scales and fin rays, alongside a mobile neck, robust ribs and a pectoral fin with wrist-like joints. Features we often discuss separately occur together in the same body.

title.zh: 同一身体上的镶嵌性状
title.en: A mosaic of features in one body

text.zh: 研究者比较骨骼的形状、位置和关节连接，判断哪些结构与其他类群相似。“镶嵌性状”指的就是不同特征组合在一起。它帮助我们研究身体结构怎样变化，却不会自动把某个化石指定为后世动物的直接祖先。
text.en: Researchers compare the shape, position and connections of bones. A mosaic of features is a combination of traits associated with different groups. It informs the study of anatomical change without identifying a fossil as a direct ancestor.

title.zh: 骨骼怎样约束运动的解释
title.en: How anatomy constrains interpretations of movement

text.zh: 骨骼可以约束运动能力的解释，但身体结构与日常行为不是同一种证据。现有描述支持这组解剖特征；不能仅凭它们断言提塔利克鱼经常在陆地上行走。阅读这类研究时，把“保存了什么”和“据此推测什么”分开，才能理解结论的分量。
text.en: Anatomy constrains interpretations of movement, but a structure and an everyday behaviour are different kinds of evidence. These descriptions support the anatomical combination; they do not establish habitual walking on land. Distinguish what is preserved from what is inferred.

readerLimitations.en: Anatomical observations, interpretations of behaviour and modelled branching times answer different questions. The selected material does not identify a direct ancestor or establish a complete distribution.
readerLimitations.zh: 解剖观察、行为解释与模型中的分支时间回答不同问题。所选材料不指定直接祖先，也不建立完整分布范围。

regionalRanges.label: Miguasha Frasnian specimen envelope
regionalRanges.basis: The named specimen and CT study provide a bounded regional occurrence context.

overview: A late Devonian elpistostegalian represented by an exceptionally complete Miguasha specimen whose pectoral fin preserves a mosaic of fin-ray anatomy and wrist- or digit-like endoskeletal elements.

ecology.diet: Unavailable from the cited pectoral-fin study
ecology.habitat: Miguasha aquatic depositional setting; finer habitat preference is unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Fin propulsion; load-bearing or digit-assisted use remains an inference
ecology.bodySize: Large-bodied elpistostegalian; a genus-wide size envelope is not inferred
ecology.guild: Unresolved aquatic predator or generalist; no feeding guild is assigned

traits: Four proximodistal radial rows in the pectoral fin
Branched carpals and distal elements interpreted as digits or putative digits
Lepidotrichia retained, confirming the appendage remained a fin
evidenceSummary: MHNM 06-2067 and CT reconstruction directly document the internal pectoral-fin architecture; digit homology and sister-group placement remain analysis-dependent, and the profile does not treat Elpistostege as a direct tetrapod ancestor.

regionalRanges.label: East Greenland Famennian limb sample
regionalRanges.basis: The described East Greenland limb specimens provide a bounded occurrence context.

overview: A Devonian tetrapod represented by East Greenland limb material that documents an eight-digit forelimb and preserves the distinction between digit-bearing limbs and evidence for terrestrial walking.

ecology.diet: Unavailable from the cited limb study
ecology.habitat: Aquatic or marginal-water setting inferred from the study context; preference unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Digit-bearing limb; terrestrial walking is not inferred from digit count alone
ecology.bodySize: Small to medium-sized early tetrapod; a study-wide mass estimate is not provided here

traits: Eight digits documented in the forelimb
Limb anatomy retains a non-pentadactyl Devonian condition
Digit-bearing limbs do not by themselves demonstrate habitual terrestrial walking
evidenceSummary: The described East Greenland limb specimens directly support eight-digit anatomy; ecological and locomotor implications remain bounded, and the profile does not infer a universal ancestral digit number or direct ancestry.

regionalRanges.label: East Greenland Famennian mobility sample
regionalRanges.basis: The named specimens and joint-mobility study provide a bounded occurrence context.

overview: A Devonian tetrapod whose three-dimensional limb reconstruction provides a bounded test of joint mobility and the mechanical requirements of a typical lateral-sequence walk.

ecology.diet: Unavailable from the cited joint-mobility study
ecology.habitat: East Greenland aquatic or marginal-water depositional setting; preference unresolved
ecology.locomotion: Restricted limb long-axis rotation in the tested reconstruction; this is not a direct observation of behaviour
ecology.bodySize: Large-bodied early tetrapod; a study-wide body-size envelope is not inferred

traits: No long-axis rotations required for a typical lateral-sequence walk in the tested model
Mobility result may be specialized to Ichthyostega rather than all early tetrapods
evidenceSummary: Micro-CT reconstruction and comparison with five living analogues constrain feasible joint motion; model assumptions and the difference between feasible motion and observed behaviour remain explicit.
